`scripts/setup.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * REVENANT first-time setup.
 *
 *   npm run setup
 *   npm run setup -- --skip-submodules
 *   npm run setup -- --full-history     (clone submodules with full git history)
 *   npm run setup -- --check            (report only; change nothing)
 *
 * What it does, in order:
 *   1. Checks prerequisites: Node.js, npm, git, CMake, a C++ compiler, QEMU.
 *   2. Initializes the native engine git submodules listed in .gitmodules.
 *   3. Creates the working directories (projects/, vm/images/).
 *   4. Generates default config files (never overwrites existing ones).
 *   5. Prints a summary and the next steps.
 *
 * Idempotent: safe to run as often as you like.
 */

import chalk from 'chalk';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { cpus, totalmem } from 'node:os';
import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
import {
  IS_WINDOWS,
  REPO_ROOT,
  capture,
  compareVersions,
  extractVersion,
  findVisualStudio,
  firstLine,
  isDirectory,
  qemuExtraDirs,
  which,
} from './lib/util.js';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Options
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Options {
  skipSubmodules: boolean;
  fullHistory: boolean;
  checkOnly: boolean;
}

function parseArgs(argv: string[]): Options {
  const opts: Options = { skipSubmodules: false, fullHistory: false, checkOnly: false };
  for (const arg of argv) {
    switch (arg) {
      case '--skip-submodules':
        opts.skipSubmodules = true;
        break;
      case '--full-history':
        opts.fullHistory = true;
        break;
      case '--check':
        opts.checkOnly = true;
        break;
      case '-h':
      case '--help':
        console.log(
          [
            'Usage: npm run setup -- [options]',
            '',
            '  --skip-submodules  do not clone the native engine submodules',
            '  --full-history     clone submodules with full history (default: shallow)',
            '  --check            only check prerequisites; create and change nothing',
          ].join('\n'),
        );
        process.exit(0);
        break;
      default:
        console.error(chalk.red(`Unknown option: ${arg}`));
        process.exit(2);
    }
  }
  return opts;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Output helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

type Status = 'ok' | 'warn' | 'fail' | 'info';

const MARK: Record<Status, string> = {
  ok: chalk.green('[ ok ]'),
  warn: chalk.yellow('[warn]'),
  fail: chalk.red('[FAIL]'),
  info: chalk.cyan('[info]'),
};

const LABEL_WIDTH = 22;

function heading(text: string): void {
  console.log(`\n${chalk.bold.underline(text)}`);
}

function line(status: Status, label: string, detail = ''): void {
  console.log(`  ${MARK[status]} ${label.padEnd(LABEL_WIDTH)} ${detail}`);
}

function hint(text: string): void {
  console.log(`         ${' '.repeat(LABEL_WIDTH)} ${chalk.dim(text)}`);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Prerequisites
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Check {
  name: string;
  status: Status;
  detail: string;
  /** Required for the TypeScript platform itself (not just optional subsystems). */
  required: boolean;
  /** The tool exists and works, even if `status` carries a warning about it. */
  usable?: boolean;
  fix?: string;
}

const MIN_NODE = '20.0.0';
const MIN_CMAKE = '3.20.0';

function checkNode(): Check {
  const version = process.versions.node;
  const ok = compareVersions(version, MIN_NODE) >= 0;
  return {
    name: 'Node.js',
    status: ok ? 'ok' : 'fail',
    detail: `v${version}${ok ? '' : ` (need >= ${MIN_NODE})`}`,
    required: true,
    fix: 'Install Node.js 20 LTS or newer from https://nodejs.org',
  };
}

function checkNpm(): Check {
  // npm sets this when the script is launched through `npm run`.
  const agent = process.env.npm_config_user_agent?.match(/npm\/(\S+)/)?.[1];
  let version = agent;
  if (!version) {
    const npmCli = process.env.npm_execpath;
    if (npmCli && existsSync(npmCli)) {
      version = extractVersion(firstLine(process.execPath, [npmCli, '--version']));
    }
  }
  if (!version && which('npm')) version = 'installed';
  return {
    name: 'npm',
    status: version ? 'ok' : 'fail',
    detail: version ? (version === 'installed' ? 'found on PATH' : `v${version}`) : 'not found',
    required: true,
    fix: 'npm ships with Node.js; reinstall Node.js',
  };
}

function checkGit(): Check {
  const version = extractVersion(firstLine('git', ['--version']));
  return {
    name: 'git',
    status: version ? 'ok' : 'fail',
    detail: version ? `v${version}` : 'not found',
    required: true,
    fix: 'Install git from https://git-scm.com',
  };
}

function checkCmake(): Check {
  const version = extractVersion(firstLine('cmake', ['--version']));
  if (!version) {
    return {
      name: 'CMake',
      status: 'warn',
      detail: 'not found (needed for `npm run build:native`)',
      required: false,
      fix: `Install CMake >= ${MIN_CMAKE} from https://cmake.org/download`,
    };
  }
  const ok = compareVersions(version, MIN_CMAKE) >= 0;
  return {
    name: 'CMake',
    status: ok ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    detail: `v${version}${ok ? '' : ` (need >= ${MIN_CMAKE})`}`,
    required: false,
    fix: `Upgrade CMake to >= ${MIN_CMAKE}`,
  };
}

function checkCompiler(): Check {
  const found: string[] = [];

  if (IS_WINDOWS) {
    const vs = findVisualStudio();
    if (vs) found.push(`MSVC (${vs.displayName} ${vs.version})`);
    if (which('cl')) found.push('cl.exe on PATH');
  }
  for (const [exe, label] of [
    ['g++', 'GCC'],
    ['clang++', 'Clang'],
  ] as const) {
    if (!which(exe)) continue;
    const version = extractVersion(firstLine(exe, ['--version']));
    found.push(`${label}${version ? ` ${version}` : ''}`);
  }

  if (found.length === 0) {
    return {
      name: 'C++ compiler',
      status: 'warn',
      detail: 'none found (needed for `npm run build:native`)',
      required: false,
      fix: IS_WINDOWS
        ? 'Install "Build Tools for Visual Studio" with the "Desktop development with C++" workload'
        : 'Install a C++20 compiler: `sudo apt install build-essential` or clang',
    };
  }
  return { name: 'C++ compiler', status: 'ok', detail: found.join(', '), required: false };
}

function checkQemu(): Check[] {
  const checks: Check[] = [];
  const extra = qemuExtraDirs();
  const qemu = which('qemu-system-x86_64', extra);
  const qemuImg = which('qemu-img', extra);

  if (!qemu) {
    checks.push({
      name: 'QEMU',
      status: 'warn',
      detail: 'qemu-system-x86_64 not found (needed for the stealth analysis VM)',
      required: false,
      fix: IS_WINDOWS
        ? 'Install QEMU for Windows (https://qemu.weilnetz.de/w64/) and add it to PATH'
        : 'Install QEMU: `sudo apt install qemu-system-x86 qemu-utils`',
    });
    return checks;
  }

  const version = extractVersion(firstLine(qemu, ['--version']));
  const onPath = Boolean(which('qemu-system-x86_64'));
  checks.push({
    name: 'QEMU',
    status: onPath ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    detail: `v${version ?? '?'} at ${qemu}${onPath ? '' : ' (not on PATH)'}`,
    required: false,
    usable: true,
    fix: onPath ? undefined : `Add ${join(qemu, '..')} to PATH so @revenant/core can find it`,
  });

  if (!qemuImg) {
    checks.push({
      name: 'qemu-img',
      status: 'warn',
      detail: 'not found (needed to create VM disks)',
      required: false,
      fix: 'qemu-img ships with QEMU; check your installation',
    });
  }

  // Hardware acceleration.
  const accelHelp = capture(qemu, ['-accel', 'help']);
  const accels = `${accelHelp.stdout}\n${accelHelp.stderr}`.toLowerCase();
  if (IS_WINDOWS) {
    const built = accels.includes('whpx');
    const hv = capture(
      'powershell.exe',
      ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', '(Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).HypervisorPresent'],
      { timeoutMs: 20_000 },
    );
    const present = hv.stdout.trim().toLowerCase() === 'true';
    if (built && present) {
      checks.push({ name: 'WHPX', status: 'ok', detail: 'supported by QEMU; Windows hypervisor is running', required: false });
    } else {
      checks.push({
        name: 'WHPX',
        status: 'warn',
        detail: !built
          ? 'this QEMU build does not list the whpx accelerator'
          : 'Windows hypervisor is not running (VMs would fall back to slow TCG)',
        required: false,
        fix: 'Elevated PowerShell: Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform, then reboot',
      });
    }
  } else if (process.platform === 'linux') {
    const kvm = existsSync('/dev/kvm');
    checks.push({
      name: 'KVM',
      status: kvm ? 'ok' : 'warn',
      detail: kvm ? '/dev/kvm present' : '/dev/kvm missing (VMs would fall back to slow TCG)',
      required: false,
      fix: kvm ? undefined : 'Enable virtualization in firmware and load the kvm module',
    });
  }
  return checks;
}

function checkHost(): Check {
  const ramGb = totalmem() / 1024 ** 3;
  const cores = cpus().length;
  const enough = ramGb >= 15 && cores >= 4;
  return {
    name: 'Host resources',
    status: enough ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    detail: `${cores} logical CPUs, ${ramGb.toFixed(0)} GB RAM`,
    required: false,
    fix: enough
      ? undefined
      : 'The default stealth VM uses 4 vCPUs / 8 GB; lower cpuCount/memoryMb in revenant.config.json',
  };
}

function runChecks(): Check[] {
  heading('Prerequisites');
  const checks = [
    checkNode(),
    checkNpm(),
    checkGit(),
    checkCmake(),
    checkCompiler(),
    ...checkQemu(),
    checkHost(),
  ];
  for (const c of checks) {
    line(c.status, c.name, c.detail);
    if (c.status !== 'ok' && c.fix) hint(c.fix);
  }
  return checks;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Git submodules
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Submodule {
  name: string;
  path: string;
  url: string;
  branch?: string;
}

type SubmoduleState = 'ready' | 'cloned' | 'failed' | 'skipped';

function parseGitmodules(): Submodule[] {
  const file = join(REPO_ROOT, '.gitmodules');
  if (!existsSync(file)) return [];
  const modules: Submodule[] = [];
  let current: Partial<Submodule> | undefined;
  const flush = (): void => {
    if (current?.name && current.path && current.url) modules.push(current as Submodule);
  };
  for (const raw of readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const text = raw.trim();
    const header = text.match(/^\[submodule\s+"(.+)"\]$/);
    if (header) {
      flush();
      current = { name: header[1] };
      continue;
    }
    const kv = text.match(/^(\w+)\s*=\s*(.+)$/);
    if (kv && current) {
      const [, key, value] = kv;
      if (key === 'path' || key === 'url' || key === 'branch') current[key] = value;
    }
  }
  flush();
  return modules;
}

function git(args: string[], timeoutMs = 60_000): ReturnType<typeof capture> {
  return capture('git', args, { cwd: REPO_ROOT, timeoutMs });
}

/**
 * The repository must be its own git work tree. `git rev-parse` alone is not
 * enough: the project may sit inside some unrelated parent repository.
 */
function isOwnGitRepo(): boolean {
  return existsSync(join(REPO_ROOT, '.git'));
}

function isPopulated(dir: string): boolean {
  if (!isDirectory(dir)) return false;
  return readdirSync(dir).some((entry) => entry !== '.gitkeep');
}

function initSubmodules(opts: Options): Map<string, SubmoduleState> {
  heading('Native engine submodules');
  const states = new Map<string, SubmoduleState>();
  const modules = parseGitmodules();

  if (modules.length === 0) {
    line('warn', '.gitmodules', 'not found or empty; nothing to initialize');
    return states;
  }
  if (opts.skipSubmodules || opts.checkOnly) {
    for (const m of modules) {
      const ready = isPopulated(join(REPO_ROOT, m.path));
      states.set(m.path, ready ? 'ready' : 'skipped');
      line(ready ? 'ok' : 'info', m.path, ready ? 'already checked out' : 'skipped');
    }
    return states;
  }
  if (!which('git')) {
    for (const m of modules) states.set(m.path, 'failed');
    line('fail', 'git', 'not available; cannot fetch submodules');
    return states;
  }

  if (!isOwnGitRepo()) {
    const init = git(['init', '--quiet']);
    if (init.code !== 0) {
      for (const m of modules) states.set(m.path, 'failed');
      line('fail', 'git init', init.stderr.trim());
      return states;
    }
    line('info', 'git init', 'initialized a git repository (submodules need one)');
  }

  for (const m of modules) {
    const dir = join(REPO_ROOT, m.path);

    if (isPopulated(dir)) {
      states.set(m.path, 'ready');
      line('ok', m.path, 'already checked out');
      continue;
    }

    // Is it already registered as a gitlink in the index?
    const staged = git(['ls-files', '--stage', '--', m.path]).stdout;
    const registered = /^160000 /m.test(staged);

    line('info', m.path, `cloning ${m.url} ...`);
    let result: ReturnType<typeof capture>;

    if (registered) {
      const args = ['submodule', 'update', '--init', '--recursive'];
      if (!opts.fullHistory) args.push('--depth', '1');
      result = git([...args, '--', m.path], 30 * 60_000);
    } else {
      // The path holds a tracked .gitkeep placeholder. `git submodule add`
      // refuses to reuse a path that is already in the index, so drop it first.
      git(['rm', '--cached', '--quiet', '--ignore-unmatch', '--', `${m.path}/.gitkeep`]);
      const keep = join(dir, '.gitkeep');
      if (existsSync(keep)) rmSync(keep);

      const args = ['submodule', 'add', '--force'];
      if (m.branch) args.push('-b', m.branch);
      if (!opts.fullHistory) args.push('--depth', '1');
      result = git([...args, '--', m.url, m.path], 30 * 60_000);

      if (result.code === 0) {
        // Engines carry their own dependencies as nested submodules (NoVmp -> VTIL, ...).
        const nested = ['submodule', 'update', '--init', '--recursive'];
        if (!opts.fullHistory) nested.push('--depth', '1');
        const sub = capture('git', nested, { cwd: dir, timeoutMs: 30 * 60_000 });
        if (sub.code !== 0) {
          line('warn', m.path, 'cloned, but nested submodules failed to initialize');
          hint(lastLine(sub.stderr));
        }
      }
    }

    if (result.code === 0 && isPopulated(dir)) {
      states.set(m.path, 'cloned');
      line('ok', m.path, 'cloned');
    } else {
      states.set(m.path, 'failed');
      line('warn', m.path, 'could not be fetched');
      hint(lastLine(result.stderr) || 'git reported no error text');
      hint(`Retry later with: git submodule add --force ${m.url} ${m.path}`);
      // Restore the placeholder so the directory survives in git.
      mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
      if (!isPopulated(dir)) writeFileSync(join(dir, '.gitkeep'), '');
    }
  }
  return states;
}

function lastLine(text: string): string {
  const lines = text
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((l) => l.trim())
    .filter(Boolean);
  return lines[lines.length - 1] ?? '';
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Directories
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const DIRECTORIES: Array<{ path: string; purpose: string }> = [
  { path: 'projects', purpose: 'analysis projects and their databases' },
  { path: 'vm/images', purpose: 'guest disk images, ISOs and firmware' },
];

function createDirectories(checkOnly: boolean): string[] {
  heading('Directories');
  const created: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, purpose } of DIRECTORIES) {
    const abs = join(REPO_ROOT, path);
    if (isDirectory(abs)) {
      line('ok', path, `exists (${purpose})`);
      continue;
    }
    if (checkOnly) {
      line('info', path, 'missing (would be created)');
      continue;
    }
    mkdirSync(abs, { recursive: true });
    // Keep the empty directory in git; its contents are ignored below.
    writeFileSync(join(abs, '.gitkeep'), '');
    created.push(path);
    line('ok', path, `created (${purpose})`);
  }
  return created;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Default configuration
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function defaultConfig(): Record<string, unknown> {
  const exe = IS_WINDOWS ? '.exe' : '';
  return {
    $comment:
      'REVENANT local configuration. Generated by `npm run setup`; edit freely. ' +
      'Paths are relative to the repository root unless absolute. null means "look on PATH".',
    version: 1,
    projectsDir: 'projects',
    native: {
      buildDir: 'native/build',
      addon: 'native/build/bin/revenant_native.node',
      tools: {
        revng: null,
        novmp: `native/build/bin/NoVmp${exe}`,
        unthemidator: `native/build/bin/unthemidator${exe}`,
      },
      timeouts: { liftMs: 1_800_000, devirtMs: 3_600_000 },
    },
    vm: {
      backend: 'qemu',
      accelerator: IS_WINDOWS ? 'whpx' : 'kvm',
      qemuPath: null,
      qemuImgPath: null,
      imagesDir: 'vm/images',
      profile: 'vm/configs/stealth-qemu.json',
      defaults: {
        name: 'revenant-stealth-win10',
        os: 'windows-10-x64',
        cpuCount: 4,
        memoryMb: 8192,
        diskMb: 61_440,
        harden: true,
      },
      agent: { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 47100 },
      stealth: {
        vmawarePath: `vm/images/vmaware${exe}`,
        guestToolsDir: 'C:\\revenant\\tools',
        maxLikelihoodPercent: 0,
      },
    },
    security: {
      $comment: 'Samples are hostile. Keep these on unless you know exactly why not.',
      neverExecuteSamplesOnHost: true,
      guestNetwork: 'isolated',
      restoreSnapshotBeforeRun: true,
    },
    logging: { level: 'info' },
  };
}

const ENV_EXAMPLE = `# REVENANT environment overrides. Copy to .env and adjust.
# Every value is optional; unset means "auto-detect".

# Explicit paths to the native engines (used by the N-API addon and @revenant/core).
# REVENANT_REVNG_PATH=
# REVENANT_NOVMP_PATH=
# REVENANT_UNTHEMIDATOR_PATH=

# Directory containing qemu-system-x86_64 / qemu-img when they are not on PATH.
# REVENANT_QEMU_DIR=

# Guest agent endpoint used by the CLI and scripts/test-vm-stealth.ts.
# REVENANT_GUEST_HOST=127.0.0.1
# REVENANT_GUEST_PORT=47100

# Host path of the VMAware CLI binary pushed into the guest by the stealth test.
# REVENANT_VMAWARE_PATH=

# Where projects are registered (defaults to ~/.revenant).
# REVENANT_HOME=
`;

const GITIGNORE_MARKER = '# REVENANT setup: local working data';
const GITIGNORE_BLOCK = `
${GITIGNORE_MARKER}
revenant.config.json
projects/*
!projects/.gitkeep
vm/images/*
!vm/images/.gitkeep
*.qcow2
*.iso
`;

function generateConfigs(checkOnly: boolean): string[] {
  heading('Configuration');
  const written: string[] = [];

  const files: Array<{ path: string; content: () => string }> = [
    {
      path: 'revenant.config.json',
      content: () => `${JSON.stringify(defaultConfig(), null, 2)}\n`,
    },
    { path: '.env.example', content: () => ENV_EXAMPLE },
  ];

  for (const file of files) {
    const abs = join(REPO_ROOT, file.path);
    if (existsSync(abs)) {
      line('ok', file.path, 'exists (left untouched)');
      continue;
    }
    if (checkOnly) {
      line('info', file.path, 'missing (would be generated)');
      continue;
    }
    writeFileSync(abs, file.content());
    written.push(file.path);
    line('ok', file.path, 'generated');
  }

  // Make sure multi-gigabyte disk images and local config never get committed.
  const gitignore = join(REPO_ROOT, '.gitignore');
  const current = existsSync(gitignore) ? readFileSync(gitignore, 'utf8') : '';
  if (current.includes(GITIGNORE_MARKER)) {
    line('ok', '.gitignore', 'working-data rules present');
  } else if (checkOnly) {
    line('info', '.gitignore', 'working-data rules missing (would be appended)');
  } else {
    writeFileSync(gitignore, `${current.replace(/\s*$/, '')}\n${GITIGNORE_BLOCK}`);
    written.push('.gitignore');
    line('ok', '.gitignore', 'appended working-data rules');
  }
  return written;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. Summary
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function summarize(
  opts: Options,
  checks: Check[],
  submodules: Map<string, SubmoduleState>,
  createdDirs: string[],
  writtenFiles: string[],
): number {
  heading('Summary');
  const failedRequired = checks.filter((c) => c.required && c.status === 'fail');
  const warnings = checks.filter((c) => c.status === 'warn');
  const has = (name: string): boolean =>
    checks.some((c) => c.name === name && (c.status === 'ok' || c.usable === true));
  const qemuOffPath = checks.some((c) => c.name === 'QEMU' && c.usable && c.status !== 'ok');

  const canBuildNative = has('CMake') && has('C++ compiler');
  const canRunVm = has('QEMU') && (has('WHPX') || has('KVM'));
  const fetched = [...submodules.values()].filter((s) => s === 'ready' || s === 'cloned').length;

  line(failedRequired.length ? 'fail' : 'ok', 'TypeScript platform', failedRequired.length ? `blocked by: ${failedRequired.map((c) => c.name).join(', ')}` : 'ready to install and build');
  line(canBuildNative ? 'ok' : 'warn', 'Native build', canBuildNative ? 'toolchain available' : 'needs CMake and a C++ compiler');
  line(
    submodules.size === 0 ? 'warn' : fetched === submodules.size ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    'Native engines',
    `${fetched}/${submodules.size} submodules checked out`,
  );
  line(
    canRunVm && !qemuOffPath ? 'ok' : 'warn',
    'Stealth VM',
    !canRunVm
      ? 'needs QEMU with WHPX/KVM'
      : qemuOffPath
        ? 'QEMU and acceleration found, but QEMU is not on PATH'
        : 'QEMU with hardware acceleration available',
  );

  if (!opts.checkOnly) {
    const changed = [...createdDirs.map((d) => `${d}/`), ...writtenFiles];
    console.log(
      `\n  ${chalk.dim('Changed:')} ${changed.length ? changed.join(', ') : 'nothing (already set up)'}`,
    );
  }
  if (warnings.length) {
    console.log(`  ${chalk.yellow(`${warnings.length} optional prerequisite(s) need attention; see above.`)}`);
  }

  heading('Next steps');
  const steps: string[] = [];
  if (failedRequired.length) steps.push('Install the missing required tools listed above, then re-run `npm run setup`.');
  if (!isDirectory(join(REPO_ROOT, 'node_modules'))) steps.push('npm install               install workspace dependencies');
  steps.push('npm run build             build the TypeScript packages');
  if (canBuildNative) {
    steps.push('npm run build:native      compile the native engines and the N-API addon');
  } else {
    steps.push('Install CMake + a C++ compiler, then `npm run build:native`.');
  }
  if (canRunVm) {
    if (qemuOffPath) steps.push('Add the QEMU directory to PATH (see the QEMU line above).');
    steps.push('Provision the guest: see vm/README.md (vm/provision/setup.ps1)');
    steps.push('npm run test:vm-stealth   validate the hardened VM against VMAware');
  } else {
    steps.push('Install QEMU and enable hardware acceleration (WHPX/KVM) to use the stealth VM.');
  }
  steps.push('Read ARCHITECTURE.md for the full system reference.');
  steps.forEach((s, i) => console.log(`  ${chalk.cyan(`${i + 1}.`)} ${s}`));
  console.log('');

  return failedRequired.length ? 1 : 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function main(): void {
  const opts = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
  console.log(chalk.bold('\nREVENANT setup'));
  console.log(chalk.dim(`  repository: ${REPO_ROOT}`));
  console.log(chalk.dim(`  platform:   ${process.platform} ${process.arch}${opts.checkOnly ? '   (check only)' : ''}`));

  const checks = runChecks();
  const submodules = initSubmodules(opts);
  const createdDirs = createDirectories(opts.checkOnly);
  const writtenFiles = generateConfigs(opts.checkOnly);
  process.exitCode = summarize(opts, checks, submodules, createdDirs, writtenFiles);
}

try {
  main();
} catch (err) {
  console.error(chalk.red(`\nSetup failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`));
  console.error(chalk.dim(`  (in ${relative(process.cwd(), REPO_ROOT) || '.'})`));
  process.exit(1);
}

```

`scripts/test-vm-stealth.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * VM stealth validation: run VMAware inside the hardened analysis VM.
 *
 *   npm run test:vm-stealth
 *   npm run test:vm-stealth -- --vm revenant-stealth-win10 --vmaware C:\tools\vmaware.exe
 *   npm run test:vm-stealth -- --create --iso D:\iso\Win10_22H2.iso
 *   npm run test:vm-stealth -- --json > stealth-report.json
 *
 * Flow
 *   1. Use the existing stealth VM (or create it with --create) through
 *      @revenant/core's VmManager, and start it if it is not running.
 *   2. Wait for the in-guest agent, then copy the VMAware CLI binary into the guest.
 *   3. Run VMAware three ways: `--detect` (VM::detect()), `--percent`
 *      (VM::percentage()) and the full per-technique report.
 *   4. Report which techniques passed (not detected) and which failed.
 *   5. Map every failed technique to a concrete hardening suggestion.
 *
 * Exit codes: 0 = undetected, 1 = detected / above threshold, 2 = could not run.
 *
 * VMAware (https://github.com/kernelwernel/VMAware) is not bundled. Build or
 * download its CLI and pass --vmaware, or set REVENANT_VMAWARE_PATH.
 */

import chalk from 'chalk';
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { isAbsolute, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { REPO_ROOT, isFile, qemuExtraDirs, which } from './lib/util.js';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The slice of @revenant/core this script relies on.
//
// Declared structurally and loaded with a dynamic import so the script gives a
// useful message when the workspace has not been built yet, and keeps working
// across the small API differences between VmManager revisions.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface VmInfoLike {
  name: string;
  state: string;
  hardened?: boolean;
  cpuCount?: number;
  memoryMb?: number;
}

interface VmManagerLike {
  isAvailable(): Promise<boolean>;
  list(): Promise<VmInfoLike[]>;
  create(options: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<VmInfoLike>;
  start(name: string, headless?: boolean): Promise<unknown>;
  stop(name: string): Promise<void>;
  restore?(name: string, snapshot: string): Promise<void>;
  restoreSnapshot?(name: string, snapshot: string): Promise<void>;
}

interface GuestResult {
  exitCode: number;
  stdout: string;
  stderr: string;
}

interface GuestAgentLike {
  connect?(host: string, port: number, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<void>;
  ping(): Promise<boolean>;
  execute?(command: { command: string; args?: string[]; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<GuestResult>;
  exec?(command: { command: string; args?: string[]; timeoutMs?: number }): Promise<GuestResult>;
  uploadFile?(localPath: string, remotePath: string): Promise<void>;
  upload?(localPath: string, remotePath: string): Promise<void>;
  close?(): void;
}

interface CoreModule {
  VmManager: new (config?: Record<string, unknown>) => VmManagerLike;
  GuestAgent?: new (config?: Record<string, unknown>) => GuestAgentLike;
  GuestAgentClient?: new (config?: Record<string, unknown>) => GuestAgentLike;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Options
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Options {
  vm: string;
  create: boolean;
  iso?: string;
  snapshot?: string;
  vmaware?: string;
  guestDir: string;
  agentHost: string;
  agentPort: number;
  bootTimeoutSec: number;
  runTimeoutSec: number;
  threshold: number;
  keepRunning: boolean;
  gui: boolean;
  json: boolean;
}

interface LocalConfig {
  vm?: {
    defaults?: { name?: string; os?: string; cpuCount?: number; memoryMb?: number; diskMb?: number };
    agent?: { host?: string; port?: number };
    stealth?: { vmawarePath?: string; guestToolsDir?: string; maxLikelihoodPercent?: number };
  };
}

function loadLocalConfig(): LocalConfig {
  const file = join(REPO_ROOT, 'revenant.config.json');
  if (!existsSync(file)) return {};
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) as LocalConfig;
  } catch {
    return {};
  }
}

function usage(): never {
  console.log(
    [
      'Usage: npm run test:vm-stealth -- [options]',
      '',
      '  --vm <name>            VM to test (default: from revenant.config.json)',
      '  --create               create the VM if it does not exist',
      '  --iso <path>           install media to attach when creating',
      '  --snapshot <name>      restore this snapshot before testing',
      '  --vmaware <path>       host path of the VMAware CLI binary',
      '  --guest-dir <path>     guest directory to copy it into (default C:\\revenant\\tools)',
      '  --agent-host <host>    guest agent host (default 127.0.0.1)',
      '  --agent-port <port>    guest agent port (default 47100)',
      '  --boot-timeout <sec>   how long to wait for the guest agent (default 300)',
      '  --run-timeout <sec>    timeout for each VMAware run (default 180)',
      '  --threshold <0-100>    highest acceptable VM::percentage() (default 0)',
      '  --keep-running         leave the VM running afterwards',
      '  --gui                  show the VM window instead of running headless',
      '  --json                 print a machine-readable report on stdout',
    ].join('\n'),
  );
  process.exit(0);
}

function parseArgs(argv: string[], config: LocalConfig): Options {
  const envPort = Number.parseInt(process.env.REVENANT_GUEST_PORT ?? '', 10);
  const opts: Options = {
    vm: config.vm?.defaults?.name ?? 'revenant-stealth-win10',
    create: false,
    vmaware: process.env.REVENANT_VMAWARE_PATH ?? config.vm?.stealth?.vmawarePath,
    guestDir: config.vm?.stealth?.guestToolsDir ?? 'C:\\revenant\\tools',
    agentHost: process.env.REVENANT_GUEST_HOST ?? config.vm?.agent?.host ?? '127.0.0.1',
    agentPort: Number.isInteger(envPort) ? envPort : (config.vm?.agent?.port ?? 47100),
    bootTimeoutSec: 300,
    runTimeoutSec: 180,
    threshold: config.vm?.stealth?.maxLikelihoodPercent ?? 0,
    keepRunning: false,
    gui: false,
    json: false,
  };

  const need = (i: number, flag: string): string => {
    const v = argv[i + 1];
    if (v === undefined) die(`${flag} requires a value`);
    return v;
  };
  const num = (i: number, flag: string, min: number, max: number): number => {
    const n = Number(need(i, flag));
    if (!Number.isFinite(n) || n < min || n > max) die(`${flag} must be between ${min} and ${max}`);
    return n;
  };

  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
    const arg = argv[i]!;
    switch (arg) {
      case '--vm': opts.vm = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--create': opts.create = true; break;
      case '--iso': opts.iso = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--snapshot': opts.snapshot = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--vmaware': opts.vmaware = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--guest-dir': opts.guestDir = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--agent-host': opts.agentHost = need(i, arg); i++; break;
      case '--agent-port': opts.agentPort = num(i, arg, 1, 65535); i++; break;
      case '--boot-timeout': opts.bootTimeoutSec = num(i, arg, 1, 3600); i++; break;
      case '--run-timeout': opts.runTimeoutSec = num(i, arg, 1, 3600); i++; break;
      case '--threshold': opts.threshold = num(i, arg, 0, 100); i++; break;
      case '--keep-running': opts.keepRunning = true; break;
      case '--gui': opts.gui = true; break;
      case '--json': opts.json = true; break;
      case '-h':
      case '--help': usage(); break;
      default: die(`Unknown option: ${arg} (try --help)`);
    }
  }
  // VM names end up in file names and monitor commands; keep them boring.
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/.test(opts.vm)) {
    die('--vm must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"');
  }
  if (opts.snapshot && !/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$/.test(opts.snapshot)) {
    die('--snapshot must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, ".", "_" or "-"');
  }
  return opts;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Output
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

let jsonMode = false;

/** Progress goes to stderr so `--json` leaves stdout clean. */
function say(text = ''): void {
  if (jsonMode) process.stderr.write(`${text}\n`);
  else console.log(text);
}

function step(text: string): void {
  say(`${chalk.cyan('>')} ${text}`);
}

/** An unrecoverable problem with the test run itself (exit code 2). */
class Fatal extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    readonly hints: string[] = [],
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}

/**
 * Abort the run. Throws instead of exiting so `finally` blocks still shut the
 * VM down; the top-level handler prints the message and exits with code 2.
 */
function die(message: string, hints: string[] = []): never {
  throw new Fatal(message, hints);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VMAware output parsing
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Technique {
  name: string;
  detected: boolean;
  /** True when VMAware could not run the check here (unsupported, disabled). */
  skipped: boolean;
}

interface VmAwareReport {
  detected: boolean | undefined;
  percentage: number | undefined;
  brand: string | undefined;
  type: string | undefined;
  techniques: Technique[];
  raw: string;
}

// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
const ANSI = /\u001b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]/g;

export function stripAnsi(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(ANSI, '');
}

/**
 * Parse the full VMAware CLI report. The exact wording changes between
 * releases, so this accepts every bracketed status form the CLI has used:
 *
 *   [  DETECTED  ] Checking CPUID hypervisor bit...
 *   [NOT DETECTED] Checking RDTSC timing...
 *   [ SKIPPED ] / [ DISABLED ] / [ NO PERMS ] / [ EASY TO SPOOF ] ...
 */
export function parseVmAwareReport(output: string): Omit<VmAwareReport, 'detected' | 'percentage'> & {
  reportedPercentage?: number;
} {
  const raw = stripAnsi(output);
  const techniques: Technique[] = [];
  let brand: string | undefined;
  let type: string | undefined;
  let reportedPercentage: number | undefined;

  for (const original of raw.split(/\r?\n/)) {
    const text = original.trim();
    if (!text) continue;

    const status = text.match(/^\[\s*([A-Za-z ]+?)\s*\]\s*(.+)$/);
    if (status) {
      const label = (status[1] ?? '').toUpperCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
      const name = (status[2] ?? '')
        .replace(/^checking\s+/i, '')
        .replace(/\.{2,}\s*$/, '')
        .trim();
      if (!name) continue;
      if (label === 'DETECTED') {
        techniques.push({ name, detected: true, skipped: false });
      } else if (label === 'NOT DETECTED') {
        techniques.push({ name, detected: false, skipped: false });
      } else if (/SKIP|DISABLED|NO PERMS|UNSUPPORTED|SPOOF/.test(label)) {
        techniques.push({ name, detected: false, skipped: true });
      }
      continue;
    }

    const kv = text.match(/^VM\s+([A-Za-z ]+?)\s*:\s*(.+)$/i);
    if (kv) {
      const key = (kv[1] ?? '').toLowerCase();
      const value = (kv[2] ?? '').trim();
      if (key === 'brand') brand = value;
      else if (key === 'type') type = value;
      else if (key === 'likeliness' || key === 'certainty' || key === 'percentage') {
        const n = Number.parseInt(value, 10);
        if (Number.isFinite(n)) reportedPercentage = n;
      }
    }
  }
  return { brand, type, techniques, raw, reportedPercentage };
}

/** `vmaware --detect` prints 1/0 (or true/false). */
export function parseDetect(output: string): boolean | undefined {
  const text = stripAnsi(output).trim().toLowerCase();
  const token = text.split(/\s+/).pop() ?? '';
  if (token === '1' || token === 'true') return true;
  if (token === '0' || token === 'false') return false;
  return undefined;
}

/** `vmaware --percent` prints an integer 0-100 (optionally with a % sign). */
export function parsePercent(output: string): number | undefined {
  const m = stripAnsi(output).match(/(\d{1,3})\s*%?\s*$/m);
  if (!m) return undefined;
  const n = Number.parseInt(m[1] ?? '', 10);
  return n >= 0 && n <= 100 ? n : undefined;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface Advice {
  area: string;
  match: RegExp;
  where: 'host (QEMU args)' | 'guest' | 'host + guest';
  fix: string;
}

      '`-cpu host,hypervisor=off,hv-vendor-id=GenuineIntel` and drop unneeded hv-* enlightenments. ' +
      'If the leaves still show, the technique cannot be closed under WHPX; test on a KVM host.',

  },

  },
  {
    area: 'ACPI',

    fix:
      'QEMU tables carry OEM ids BOCHS/BXPC. Override them (`-acpitable` / machine `x-oem-id`, `x-oem-table-id`) ' +

  },
  {
    area: 'Network / MAC',
    match: /mac address|\bmac\b|oui|network adapter|nic|ethernet|adapter/i,
    where: 'host (QEMU args)',
    fix:
      'The default 52:54:00 prefix identifies QEMU. Use a real vendor OUI (`-device e1000e,mac=d8:5e:d3:..`) ' +
      'and prefer e1000e over virtio-net so no Red Hat PCI vendor id (1AF4) appears.',
  },
  {
    area: 'Disk / storage',
    match: /disk|hdd|drive|storage|serial number|scsi|ide|ahci|nvme|volume|partition|harddisk|dvd|cd-?rom/i,
    where: 'host (QEMU args)',
    fix:
      'Replace "QEMU HARDDISK"/"QEMU DVD-ROM" with `-device ide-hd,model=<real model>,serial=<serial>` ' +
      '(or an emulated NVMe with model/serial set), remove unused optical drives, and size the disk at ' +
      '>= 120 GB: small disks are scored as sandboxes.',
  },
  {
    area: 'Display / GPU',
    match: /gpu|vga|display|video|graphics|monitor|resolution|edid|screen|directx|opengl|vulkan/i,
    where: 'host + guest',
    fix:
      'The std/Bochs VGA adapter reports "Microsoft Basic Display Adapter" and vendor 1234:1111. Supply a ' +
      'real EDID and resolution, or pass through a GPU. This is the hardest category to close without passthrough.',
  },
  {
    area: 'PCI / device inventory',
    match: /pci|device|vendor id|virtio|1af4|1b36|red hat|usb|hid|pnp|setupapi|device manager/i,
    where: 'host + guest',
    fix:
      'Remove virtio/QXL/SPICE devices (PCI vendors 1AF4, 1B36) from the command line and use emulated ' +
      'Intel hardware (q35, e1000e, ich9-ahci, usb-ehci). Then run the guest agent hardening pass to ' +

  },
  {
    area: 'Registry',
    match: /registry|regkey|reg key|hklm|hkey|systembiosversion|videobiosversion/i,
    where: 'guest',
    fix:
      'Run the guest hardening pass (agent `applyHardening` / GuestHardening.patchRegistry): remove guest-tool ' +
      'keys and rewrite HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System BIOS strings. Re-run after driver installs, which re-create them.',
  },
  {

    match: /driver|service|\.sys|\.dll|file|directory|path|qemu-ga|guest agent|vioserial|balloon|spice|vbox|vmware|tools/i,
    where: 'guest',
    fix:
      'Do not install virtio drivers, qemu-ga or SPICE tools in the image. Run GuestHardening.cleanupServices and ' +

    where: 'guest',
    fix:
      'A helper process or window class is visible. Rename the REVENANT agent binary and its scheduled task to ' +
      'something unremarkable and stop analysis tools before the sample starts (GuestHardening.hideProcesses).',
  },
  {
    area: 'WMI',
    match: /wmi|win32_|cim|computersystem|msacpi|wbem/i,
    where: 'host + guest',
    fix:
      'WMI classes are populated from SMBIOS, so fix the host-side `-smbios` values first. Then run ' +
      'GuestHardening.patchWmi for values Windows caches (OEMInformation, Win32_ComputerSystem model).',
  },
  {
    area: 'Memory / resources',
    match: /memory|ram|uptime|cursor|mouse|user activity|idle|recent files|wallpaper|username|hostname|computer name|locale|language/i,
    where: 'host + guest',
    fix:
      'Sandbox heuristics: give the VM >= 8 GB RAM and >= 4 cores, a normal user/host name, real uptime before ' +
      'testing, and a lived-in profile (documents, browser history, moved cursor).',
  },
  {
    area: 'Audio / peripherals',
    match: /audio|sound|speaker|microphone|printer|bluetooth|webcam|camera|sensor/i,
    where: 'host (QEMU args)',
    fix:
      'Machines without any audio endpoint look virtual. Add `-device ich9-intel-hda -device hda-duplex` and a ' +
      'USB tablet/keyboard; the profile sets "audio": "none", which should be changed.',
  },
  {
    area: 'Instruction behaviour',
    match: /sidt|sgdt|sldt|smsw|str\b|invalid opcode|vmx|vmcall|vmmcall|xgetbv|port|in instruction|backdoor|trap|single.?step|interrupt/i,
    where: 'host (QEMU args)',
    fix:
      'These probe how privileged or undefined instructions behave. They pass under hardware virtualization ' +
      '(WHPX/KVM) and fail under TCG: confirm the VM is really running with `accel=whpx`, not the TCG fallback.',
  },
];

function adviceFor(technique: string): Advice {
  return (
    ADVICE.find((a) => a.match.test(technique)) ?? {
      area: 'Uncategorized',
      match: /./,
      where: 'host + guest',
      fix:
        'No rule matches this technique yet. Look it up in the VMAware documentation (docs/documentation.md lists ' +
        'what each technique reads), then add a rule to ADVICE in scripts/test-vm-stealth.ts.',
    }
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Guest helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
}

async function connectAgent(core: CoreModule, opts: Options): Promise<GuestAgentLike> {
  const Agent = core.GuestAgent ?? core.GuestAgentClient;
  if (!Agent) die('@revenant/core does not export GuestAgent.');

  const deadline = Date.now() + opts.bootTimeoutSec * 1000;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  let attempts = 0;

  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    attempts++;
    const agent = new Agent({ host: opts.agentHost, port: opts.agentPort });
    try {
      if (agent.connect) await agent.connect(opts.agentHost, opts.agentPort, 5_000);
      if (await agent.ping()) return agent;
      lastError = 'connected, but ping was not answered';
    } catch (err) {
      lastError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
    }
    agent.close?.();
    if (attempts === 1) say(chalk.dim(`  waiting for the guest agent (up to ${opts.bootTimeoutSec}s) ...`));
    await sleep(3_000);
  }

  die(`The guest agent at ${opts.agentHost}:${opts.agentPort} did not respond (${lastError}).`, [
    'Check that the guest has finished booting and the agent task is running (vm/provision/agent-install.ps1).',
    'With QEMU user-mode networking the agent port must be forwarded to the host:',
    `  -netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:${opts.agentPort}-:${opts.agentPort}`,
    'Override the endpoint with --agent-host/--agent-port or REVENANT_GUEST_HOST/REVENANT_GUEST_PORT.',
  ]);
}

async function guestExec(
  agent: GuestAgentLike,
  command: string,
  args: string[],
  timeoutMs: number,
): Promise<GuestResult> {
  const run = agent.execute?.bind(agent) ?? agent.exec?.bind(agent);
  if (!run) die('The guest agent client has no execute() method.');
  return run({ command, args, timeoutMs });
}

async function guestUpload(agent: GuestAgentLike, local: string, remote: string): Promise<void> {
  const upload = agent.uploadFile?.bind(agent) ?? agent.upload?.bind(agent);
  if (!upload) die('The guest agent client has no uploadFile() method.');
  await upload(local, remote);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reporting
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

interface StealthVerdict {
  vm: string;
  pass: boolean;
  detected: boolean | undefined;
  percentage: number | undefined;
  threshold: number;
  brand: string | undefined;
  type: string | undefined;
  counts: { total: number; passed: number; failed: number; skipped: number };
  failed: Array<{ technique: string; area: string; where: string; fix: string }>;
  passed: string[];
  skipped: string[];
  notes: string[];
}

function buildVerdict(opts: Options, report: VmAwareReport): StealthVerdict {
  const failed = report.techniques.filter((t) => t.detected);
  const skipped = report.techniques.filter((t) => t.skipped);
  const passed = report.techniques.filter((t) => !t.detected && !t.skipped);
  const notes: string[] = [];

  if (report.detected === undefined) notes.push('VM::detect() output could not be parsed; verdict relies on percentage and techniques.');
  if (report.percentage === undefined) notes.push('VM::percentage() output could not be parsed.');
  if (report.techniques.length === 0) {
    notes.push('No per-technique lines were recognized; this VMAware build may use a different report format.');
  }

  // Unknown never counts as a pass: a result we could not read is not evidence of stealth.
  const detectOk = report.detected === false;
  const percentOk = report.percentage !== undefined && report.percentage <= opts.threshold;
  const pass = detectOk && percentOk;

  return {
    vm: opts.vm,
    pass,
    detected: report.detected,
    percentage: report.percentage,
    threshold: opts.threshold,
    brand: report.brand,
    type: report.type,
    counts: {
      total: report.techniques.length,
      passed: passed.length,
      failed: failed.length,
      skipped: skipped.length,
    },
    failed: failed.map((t) => {
      const a = adviceFor(t.name);
      return { technique: t.name, area: a.area, where: a.where, fix: a.fix };
    }),
    passed: passed.map((t) => t.name),
    skipped: skipped.map((t) => t.name),
    notes,
  };
}

function printVerdict(v: StealthVerdict): void {
  const rule = chalk.dim('-'.repeat(72));
  console.log(`\n${chalk.bold('VMAware results')}  ${chalk.dim(v.vm)}`);
  console.log(rule);

  const detectText =
    v.detected === undefined
      ? chalk.yellow('unknown')
      : v.detected
        ? chalk.red('true  (virtual machine detected)')
        : chalk.green('false (not detected)');
  const pctText =
    v.percentage === undefined
      ? chalk.yellow('unknown')
      : (v.percentage <= v.threshold ? chalk.green : chalk.red)(`${v.percentage}%`) +
        chalk.dim(`  (threshold ${v.threshold}%)`);

  console.log(`  VM::detect()       ${detectText}`);
  console.log(`  VM::percentage()   ${pctText}`);
  if (v.brand) console.log(`  VM::brand()        ${/unknown|none/i.test(v.brand) ? chalk.green(v.brand) : chalk.red(v.brand)}`);
  if (v.type) console.log(`  VM::type()         ${v.type}`);
  console.log(
    `  techniques         ${chalk.green(`${v.counts.passed} passed`)}, ` +
      `${(v.counts.failed ? chalk.red : chalk.green)(`${v.counts.failed} failed`)}, ` +
      `${chalk.dim(`${v.counts.skipped} skipped`)} of ${v.counts.total}`,
  );

  if (v.failed.length) {
    console.log(`\n${chalk.bold.red('Failed checks')} ${chalk.dim('(the guest was identified as a VM)')}`);
    for (const f of v.failed) console.log(`  ${chalk.red('FAIL')}  ${f.technique} ${chalk.dim(`[${f.area}]`)}`);
  }
  if (v.passed.length) {
    console.log(`\n${chalk.bold.green('Passed checks')}`);
    for (const name of v.passed) console.log(`  ${chalk.green('pass')}  ${name}`);
  }
  if (v.skipped.length) {
    console.log(`\n${chalk.bold('Skipped by VMAware')}`);
    for (const name of v.skipped) console.log(`  ${chalk.dim('skip')}  ${chalk.dim(name)}`);
  }

  if (v.failed.length) {
    console.log(`\n${chalk.bold('Hardening suggestions')}`);
    // One suggestion per area, listing the techniques it would address.
    const byArea = new Map<string, { where: string; fix: string; techniques: string[] }>();
    for (const f of v.failed) {
      const entry = byArea.get(f.area) ?? { where: f.where, fix: f.fix, techniques: [] };
      entry.techniques.push(f.technique);
      byArea.set(f.area, entry);
    }
    let n = 1;
    for (const [area, entry] of byArea) {
      console.log(`\n  ${chalk.cyan(`${n++}.`)} ${chalk.bold(area)} ${chalk.dim(`- fix on: ${entry.where}`)}`);
      console.log(`     ${chalk.dim('triggers:')} ${entry.techniques.join('; ')}`);
      console.log(`     ${entry.fix}`);
    }
    console.log(
      chalk.dim(
        '\n  Host-side values live in vm/configs/stealth-qemu.json and packages/core/src/vm/hardening.ts;\n' +
          '  guest-side fixes in vm/agent/src/guest-hardening.ts. Re-run this test after every change.',
      ),
    );
  }

  for (const note of v.notes) console.log(chalk.yellow(`\n  note: ${note}`));

  console.log(`\n${rule}`);
  console.log(
    v.pass
      ? chalk.green.bold('  STEALTH OK: VMAware did not identify the guest as a virtual machine.')
      : chalk.red.bold('  STEALTH FAILED: the guest is detectable. Apply the suggestions above and re-test.'),
  );
  console.log('');
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

async function loadCore(): Promise<CoreModule> {
  try {
    return (await import('@revenant/core')) as unknown as CoreModule;
  } catch (err) {
    die('Could not load @revenant/core.', [
      'Run `npm install && npm run build` at the repository root first.',
      `(${err instanceof Error ? err.message.split('\n')[0] : String(err)})`,
    ]);
  }
}

async function main(): Promise<number> {
  const config = loadLocalConfig();
  const opts = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2), config);
  jsonMode = opts.json;

  say(chalk.bold('\nREVENANT VM stealth test'));

  // --- Preconditions -------------------------------------------------------
  if (!opts.vmaware) {
    die('No VMAware binary configured.', [
      'Build or download the VMAware CLI (https://github.com/kernelwernel/VMAware/releases),',
      'then pass --vmaware <path> or set REVENANT_VMAWARE_PATH.',
    ]);
  }
  const vmawareHost = isAbsolute(opts.vmaware) ? opts.vmaware : resolve(REPO_ROOT, opts.vmaware);
  if (!isFile(vmawareHost)) {
    die(`VMAware binary not found: ${vmawareHost}`, [
      'Build or download the VMAware CLI (https://github.com/kernelwernel/VMAware/releases),',
      'then pass --vmaware <path> or set REVENANT_VMAWARE_PATH.',
    ]);
  }

  const core = await loadCore();
  // QEMU for Windows is usually installed outside PATH; point VmManager at it.
  const qemuDirs = qemuExtraDirs();
  const vm = new core.VmManager({
    qemuPath: which('qemu-system-x86_64', qemuDirs),
    qemuImgPath: which('qemu-img', qemuDirs),
  });
  if (!(await vm.isAvailable())) {
    die('QEMU (qemu-system-x86_64) is not available.', [
      'Install QEMU and make sure it is on PATH; `npm run setup -- --check` shows what is missing.',
    ]);
  }

  // --- 1. Create or reuse the VM ------------------------------------------
  let info = (await vm.list()).find((v) => v.name === opts.vm);
  if (!info) {
    if (!opts.create) {
      const known = (await vm.list()).map((v) => v.name);
      die(`VM "${opts.vm}" does not exist.`, [
        known.length ? `Known VMs: ${known.join(', ')}` : 'No VMs are defined yet.',
        'Pass --create to define it, or provision one with vm/provision/setup.ps1.',
      ]);
    }
    if (opts.iso && !isFile(opts.iso)) die(`Install media not found: ${opts.iso}`);
    step(`Creating hardened VM "${opts.vm}"`);
    const d = config.vm?.defaults ?? {};
    info = await vm.create({
      name: opts.vm,
      os: d.os ?? 'windows-10-x64',
      cpuCount: d.cpuCount ?? 4,
      memoryMb: d.memoryMb ?? 8192,
      diskMb: d.diskMb ?? 61_440,
      isoPath: opts.iso,
      harden: true,
    });
    die(`VM "${opts.vm}" was created with an empty disk.`, [
      'Install Windows and the guest agent first (see vm/README.md, vm/provision/setup.ps1),',
      'then run this test again without --create.',
    ]);
  }
  step(`Using VM "${info.name}" (${info.state}${info.hardened === false ? ', NOT hardened' : ', hardened'})`);
  if (info.hardened === false) {
    say(chalk.yellow('  This VM was created without hardening; expect it to be detected.'));
  }

  let startedHere = false;
  if (info.state !== 'running') {
    step(`Starting ${opts.vm} ${opts.gui ? '' : '(headless)'}`);
    await vm.start(opts.vm, !opts.gui);
    startedHere = true;
  }

  let agent: GuestAgentLike | undefined;
  try {
    if (opts.snapshot) {
      step(`Restoring snapshot "${opts.snapshot}"`);
      const restore = vm.restore?.bind(vm) ?? vm.restoreSnapshot?.bind(vm);
      if (!restore) die('This VmManager cannot restore snapshots.');
      await restore(opts.vm, opts.snapshot);
    }

    // --- 2. Copy VMAware into the guest -----------------------------------
    step(`Connecting to the guest agent at ${opts.agentHost}:${opts.agentPort}`);
    agent = await connectAgent(core, opts);

    const guestDir = opts.guestDir.replace(/[\\/]+$/, '');
    const guestExe = `${guestDir}\\vmaware.exe`;
    step(`Copying VMAware into the guest (${guestExe})`);
    await guestExec(agent, 'cmd.exe', ['/d', '/c', 'mkdir', guestDir], 30_000).catch(() => undefined);
    await guestUpload(agent, vmawareHost, guestExe);

    // --- 3. Run VMAware ----------------------------------------------------
    const timeoutMs = opts.runTimeoutSec * 1000;
    step('Running VM::detect()');
    const detectRun = await guestExec(agent, guestExe, ['--detect'], timeoutMs);
    step('Running VM::percentage()');
    const percentRun = await guestExec(agent, guestExe, ['--percent'], timeoutMs);
    step('Running the full technique report');
    const fullRun = await guestExec(agent, guestExe, [], timeoutMs);

    if (!fullRun.stdout.trim() && !detectRun.stdout.trim()) {
      die('VMAware produced no output in the guest.', [
        `exit code ${fullRun.exitCode}; stderr: ${fullRun.stderr.trim().slice(0, 300) || '(empty)'}`,
        'Check that the binary matches the guest architecture and that its runtime DLLs are present.',
      ]);
    }

    const parsed = parseVmAwareReport(`${fullRun.stdout}\n${fullRun.stderr}`);
    const report: VmAwareReport = {
      detected: parseDetect(detectRun.stdout),
      percentage: parsePercent(percentRun.stdout) ?? parsed.reportedPercentage,
      brand: parsed.brand,
      type: parsed.type,
      techniques: parsed.techniques,
      raw: parsed.raw,
    };

    // --- 4 + 5. Report and advise -----------------------------------------
    const verdict = buildVerdict(opts, report);
    if (opts.json) {
      process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ ...verdict, raw: report.raw }, null, 2)}\n`);
    } else {
      printVerdict(verdict);
    }
    return verdict.pass ? 0 : 1;
  } finally {
    agent?.close?.();
    if (startedHere && !opts.keepRunning) {
      step(`Stopping ${opts.vm}`);
      await vm.stop(opts.vm).catch((err: unknown) => {
        say(chalk.yellow(`  could not stop the VM cleanly: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`));
      });
    }
  }
}

// Only run when executed directly, so the parsers can be imported by tests.
const invoked = process.argv[1] ? resolve(process.argv[1]) : '';
if (/test-vm-stealth\.[cm]?[jt]s$/.test(invoked)) {
  main().then(
    (code) => {
      process.exitCode = code;
    },
    (err: unknown) => {
      if (err instanceof Fatal) {
        process.stderr.write(chalk.red(`\n${err.message}\n`));
        for (const h of err.hints) process.stderr.write(chalk.dim(`  ${h}\n`));
      } else {
        process.stderr.write(
          chalk.red(`\nStealth test failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}\n`),
        );
      }
      process.exitCode = 2;
    },
  );
}

`vm/README.md`:

```md
# REVENANT VM layer

A lightweight, stealth Windows 10 analysis VM for the REVENANT reverse
engineering platform. It is **not** VirtualBox — it is **QEMU + WHPX** (Windows
Hypervisor Platform), chosen for a small footprint, fast boot, and a much larger
spoofing surface than consumer VM products expose.

The goal is to defeat anti-analysis / anti-VM checks the way the
[VMAware](https://github.com/NotRequiem/VMAware) library performs them — roughly
90 techniques spanning CPUID, SMBIOS/DMI, ACPI tables, RDTSC timing, registry
keys, MAC OUIs, disk identifiers, driver/service names, firmware strings, and
running processes — so that samples which refuse to run under instrumentation
behave as they would on bare metal.

> REVENANT is a defensive RE/malware-analysis platform. The VM exists so that
> analysts can observe evasive samples in a controlled sandbox.

---

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────── HOST (Windows 11 + QEMU/WHPX) ─────────────────────────┐
│                                                                                 │
│   provision/harden.ps1 ──reads──> configs/stealth-qemu.json                     │
│         │  (generates spoofed QEMU command line: SMBIOS/ACPI/CPUID/disk/MAC)    │
│         ▼                                                                        │
│   qemu-system-x86_64 -accel whpx ...                                            │
│         │                                                                        │
│         │   WebSocket JSON-RPC (ws://guest:47100)                               │
│         ▼                                                                        │
│  ┌──────────────── GUEST (Windows 10) ────────────────┐                         │
│  │  @revenant/vm-agent (SYSTEM scheduled task)         │                         │
│  │    ├─ execute / upload / download                   │                         │
│  │    ├─ DriverLoader   (sc.exe create/start)          │                         │
│  │    ├─ ProcessMonitor (tasklist / Get-Process)       │                         │
│  │    ├─ GuestHardening (registry/service/WMI cleanup) │                         │
│  │    └─ runVmAwareTest (vmaware.exe)                   │                         │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Hardening is split deliberately into two halves:

| Half | Where | What it fixes |
|------|-------|---------------|
| **Host-side** | `harden.ps1` → QEMU args | Firmware-level tells the guest cannot change: CPUID hypervisor bit, HV vendor id, SMBIOS/DMI tables, ACPI OEM ids, disk model/serial, MAC OUI, RTC. |
| **Guest-side** | agent `GuestHardening` / in-guest pass | Software artifacts left by generic images: guest-tool registry keys, services, drivers, files, WMI/OEM values, VM-branded PnP devices, running helper processes. |

Neither half alone is sufficient — VMAware probes both layers.

---

## Detection categories covered

| Category | Technique | Countered by |
|----------|-----------|--------------|
| CPUID | hypervisor-present bit (leaf 1, ecx[31]) | `-cpu host,-hypervisor` |
| CPUID | HV vendor string ("KVMKVMKVM", "TCGTCGTCGTCG", "Microsoft Hv") | `hv_vendor_id=GenuineIntel` |
| SMBIOS / DMI | BIOS vendor/version/date (type 0) | `-smbios type=0,...` (AMI, 2601) |
| SMBIOS / DMI | system manufacturer/product (type 1) | `-smbios type=1,...` (ASUS PRIME B550-PLUS) |
| SMBIOS / DMI | baseboard (type 2), chassis (type 3), CPU (type 4) | `-smbios type=2/3/4,...` |
| ACPI | OEM id / table id ("BOCHS", "BXPC") | `-acpitable oem_id=ALASKA,oem_table_id=A M I` |
| Disk | "QEMU HARDDISK" / "VBOX HARDDISK" model & serial | `-device ide-hd,model=Samsung SSD 970 EVO Plus 1TB,serial=...` |
| Network | VM MAC OUIs (52:54:00 QEMU, 08:00:27 VBox, 00:0C:29 VMware) | `mac=` with real ASUS/Intel OUI |
| Timing | RDTSC drift, localtime | `-rtc base=localtime,clock=host`, WHPX native TSC |
| Registry | Oracle/VMware tool keys, ACPI `VBOX__`, BIOS strings, service keys | `GuestHardening.patchRegistry` |
| Services/drivers | VBoxGuest/Mouse/SF/Video, vmci/vmhgfs/vmmouse, qemu-ga, virtio, spice | `GuestHardening.cleanupServices` |
| Filesystem | guest-addition dirs, `VBox*.dll/.sys`, virtio/vmware drivers | `GuestHardening.cleanupFilesystem` |
| WMI / OEM | Win32_BIOS/BaseBoard/ComputerSystem, OEMInformation | `GuestHardening.patchWmi` |
| Processes | VBoxTray/Service, vmtoolsd, qemu-ga, spice-vdagent | `GuestHardening.hideProcesses` |
| Devices | VM-branded PnP devices, disk friendly-name | `GuestHardening.cleanupDevices` |

---

## Provisioning a new VM

Prerequisites on the host:

- **QEMU for Windows** (qemu.weilnetz.de) in `C:\Program Files\qemu` (or pass `-QemuDir`).
- **WHPX enabled**: `Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName HypervisorPlatform`.
- A **Windows 10 x64 ISO** (or `-DownloadIso` to fetch the Media Creation Tool).
- Optionally **mtools** (`mformat`/`mcopy`) to build the unattended config floppy.

Steps:

```powershell
# 1. Build the guest agent (produces agent/dist, bundled onto the config drive)
cd vm\agent
npm install
npm run build

# 2. Initial unattended OS install
cd ..\provision
.\setup.ps1 -IsoPath D:\iso\Win10_22H2.iso
#   -> creates work\analysis-disk.qcow2
#   -> builds the autounattend config floppy (answer file + agent-install.ps1 + agent\dist)
#   -> boots QEMU/WHPX; Windows installs unattended and auto-runs agent-install.ps1

# 3. Generate the stealth launch command for day-to-day runs
.\harden.ps1 -Report
#   -> work\launch-stealth.cmd  (fully spoofed QEMU command)
#   -> work\vmaware-coverage.md (what each arg covers)

# 4. Boot the hardened VM
.\harden.ps1 -Run
```

`unattend.xml` drives the install: generic Win10 Pro key (install-only),
auto-partition, OOBE skipped, local admin `analyst`, RDP + PowerShell remoting
on, timezone set, Windows Update disabled, test signing enabled (so analysis
drivers can load), and the agent installed on first logon.

> The admin password in `unattend.xml` is a placeholder — replace it before any
> non-local use. Do not reuse it outside the isolated analysis network.

---

## Guest agent communication

The agent (`@revenant/vm-agent`) runs as a SYSTEM scheduled task inside the
guest and listens on `ws://0.0.0.0:47100`. The host connects and speaks
**JSON-RPC 2.0** over the single WebSocket:

```jsonc
// request
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "execute",
  "params": { "command": "whoami", "shell": "powershell" } }
// response
{ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "exitCode": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "" } }
```

Methods:

| Method | Params | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `ping` | — | liveness |
| `execute` | `command`, `cwd?`, `timeout?`, `shell?` | run a command (powershell/cmd) |
| `upload` | `path`, `data` (base64) | host → guest file write |
| `download` | `path` | guest → host file read (base64) |
| `loadDriver` | `path`, `name?` | register+start a kernel driver via sc.exe |
| `unloadDriver` | `name` | stop+delete the driver service |
| `listDrivers` | — | `driverquery` enumeration |
| `listProcesses` | — | `tasklist /FO CSV` |
| `monitorProcess` | `target` (name or pid) | modules, threads, memory |
| `injectDll` | `pid`, `dllPath` | DLL-injection hook (native helper stub) |
| `applyHardening` | `only?` (categories) | run the in-guest hardening pass |
| `runVmAwareTest` | `binary?` | run vmaware.exe, return verdict |
| `shutdown` | — | exit the agent |

The port is configurable via `--port=<n>` or `REVENANT_AGENT_PORT`. Keep the
control channel on a host-only network; `agent-install.ps1` opens only that TCP
port on the guest firewall.

---

## Running VMAware tests

1. Build/obtain `vmaware.exe` from the VMAware repo.
2. Upload it: `upload { path: "C:\\revenant\\tools\\vmaware.exe", data: <b64> }`.
3. Run: `runVmAwareTest { binary: "C:\\revenant\\tools\\vmaware.exe" }`.

The agent returns the raw output plus a parsed `detectedAsVm` flag. Target: **0
detections**. Any residual hit tells you which layer still leaks — re-check the
corresponding row in the coverage table and the generated
`work/vmaware-coverage.md`.

Typical loop:

```
harden.ps1 -Run  →  (guest) applyHardening  →  runVmAwareTest  →  inspect hits  →  adjust config/guest pass  →  repeat
```

---

vm/

│   ├── package.json           # @revenant/vm-agent, deps: ws

│   └── src/

---

## Notes & limitations

- **WHPX vs KVM**: WHPX does not expose every SMBIOS/ACPI knob the Linux/KVM
  stack does; the args here are the subset WHPX honors. If a category still
  leaks, confirm your QEMU build supports `-smbios type=N` / `-acpitable` on
  Windows.
- **Driver loading** needs test signing (set by `unattend.xml`) or a signed
  analysis driver.
- **DLL injection** (`injectDll`) is a validated stub: it confirms the target
  and intended technique (CreateRemoteThread + LoadLibraryW) but defers the
  actual remote write to a native helper the host uploads.
- Keep the analysis VM on an **isolated network**. Disabled Windows Update and
  loaded samples mean it must never touch a production LAN.

```

`vm/agent/src/driver-loader.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * DriverLoader — kernel driver management inside the guest.
 *
 * Uses the native Service Control Manager via `sc.exe` to register a kernel
 * driver as a service and start it, which is the standard way to load an
 * unsigned/analysis driver on a test-signing or DSE-disabled guest. The
 * REVENANT host provisions the guest with test signing enabled, so these
 * drivers (e.g. the API-monitor callback driver) can load.
 *
 * All operations shell out and parse text output — there is no native Node
 * binding for the SCM, and sc.exe is always present on Windows.
 */

import { exec } from "node:child_process";
import { promisify } from "node:util";
import path from "node:path";

const execAsync = promisify(exec);

export interface DriverLoadResult {
  name: string;
  path: string;
  created: boolean;
  started: boolean;
  log: string[];
}

export interface DriverUnloadResult {
  name: string;
  stopped: boolean;
  deleted: boolean;
  log: string[];
}

export interface LoadedDriver {
  moduleName: string;
  displayName: string;
  driverType: string;
  linkDate: string;
}

export class DriverLoader {
  /**
   * Register and start a kernel driver.
   *
   * @param driverPath absolute path to the .sys file inside the guest
   * @param name       optional service name; defaults to the .sys basename
   */
  async loadDriver(driverPath: string, name?: string): Promise<DriverLoadResult> {
    const serviceName = name ?? path.basename(driverPath).replace(/\.sys$/i, "");
    const log: string[] = [];

    // `binPath=` requires the space after `=` to be absent and the value
    // quoted. sc.exe is picky about the `key= value` form.
    const createCmd = `sc.exe create ${quote(serviceName)} type= kernel start= demand binPath= ${quote(
      driverPath,
    )}`;
    const created = await this.run(createCmd, log);

    let started = false;
    if (created) {
      const startCmd = `sc.exe start ${quote(serviceName)}`;
      started = await this.run(startCmd, log);
    }

    return { name: serviceName, path: driverPath, created, started, log };
  }

  /**
   * Stop and remove a previously loaded driver service.
   */
  async unloadDriver(name: string): Promise<DriverUnloadResult> {
    const log: string[] = [];
    const stopped = await this.run(`sc.exe stop ${quote(name)}`, log);
    const deleted = await this.run(`sc.exe delete ${quote(name)}`, log);
    return { name, stopped, deleted, log };
  }

  /**
   * Enumerate currently loaded kernel drivers via driverquery.
   * CSV output is parsed into structured records.
   */
  async listLoadedDrivers(): Promise<LoadedDriver[]> {
    const { stdout } = await execAsync(
      "driverquery /FO CSV /NH /V",
      { windowsHide: true, maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024 },
    ).catch(() => ({ stdout: "" }));

    const rows: LoadedDriver[] = [];
    for (const line of stdout.split(/\r?\n/)) {
      if (!line.trim()) continue;
      const cols = parseCsvLine(line);
      if (cols.length < 2) continue;
      // /V columns: Module Name, Display Name, Description, Driver Type, ...,
      // Link Date (col index varies by locale). Keep the robust subset.
      rows.push({
        moduleName: cols[0] ?? "",
        displayName: cols[1] ?? "",
        driverType: cols[3] ?? "",
        linkDate: cols[cols.length - 1] ?? "",
      });
    }
    return rows;
  }

  private async run(cmd: string, log: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
    try {
      const { stdout, stderr } = await execAsync(cmd, {
        windowsHide: true,
        maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 * 1024,
      });
      log.push(`$ ${cmd}`);
      if (stdout.trim()) log.push(stdout.trim());
      if (stderr.trim()) log.push(stderr.trim());
      // sc.exe reports success in stdout ("SUCCESS") and nonzero exit on error.
      return true;
    } catch (err: unknown) {
      const e = err as { stdout?: string; stderr?: string; message?: string };
      log.push(`$ ${cmd}`);
      log.push(`ERROR: ${e.stderr?.trim() || e.stdout?.trim() || e.message || String(err)}`);
      return false;
    }
  }
}

function quote(value: string): string {
  return `"${value.replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
}

/** Minimal RFC-4180-ish CSV line parser (handles quoted fields with commas). */
function parseCsvLine(line: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  let cur = "";
  let inQuotes = false;
  for (let i = 0; i < line.length; i++) {
    const ch = line[i];
    if (inQuotes) {
      if (ch === '"' && line[i + 1] === '"') {
        cur += '"';
        i++;
      } else if (ch === '"') {
        inQuotes = false;
      } else {
        cur += ch;
      }
    } else if (ch === '"') {
      inQuotes = true;
    } else if (ch === ",") {
      out.push(cur);
      cur = "";
    } else {
      cur += ch;
    }
  }
  out.push(cur);
  return out;
}
